newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - January 14.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Tuesday's edition of Daily Variety:

HOLLYWOOD - Warner Bros, of Time Warner Inc, is in talks with Burger King, of Grand Metropolitan, about a first-look arrangement to be the promotional partner on the long-in-development Superman Reborn, which the studio is preparing for summer 1998.

NEW ORLEANS - Silver King and Home Shopping Network CEO Barry Diller called on the television industry to cover the broadcast advertising costs of all government candidates as a means to overhaul the current system of political contributions.

NEW ORLEANS - It's a statistic that has stunned the industry: for the first time ever, no distributor at NATPE is pushing any fall 1997 pilots specifically aimed at weekday prime access, the most lucrative time period in TV syndication.

NEW YORK - Two-time Oscar-winning director Milos Forman has agreed to make The Little Black Book his next film. Forman, who ended a five-year hiatus with The People vs. Larry Flynt, expects to begin shooting the film for Universal in the fall.

HOLLYWOOD - Jeff Robinov, who has been an agent with International Creative Management for the past three years, handling the careers of young, hot writer-directors, is leaving to become senior VP of production at Warner Bros.
